payload.content: Running `node -e "..."` with the script wrapped in double quotes causes bash itself to interpret JS template-literal `${...}` expressions as shell parameter expansions, producing errors like `${item.scenario.slug||item.scenario.id}: bad substitution` (also seen for `${item.scenario.name}` and `${item.count_objects}`) before node ever runs the code. Wrapping the same `-e` script in single quotes instead passes it to node unmodified and the command runs cleanly.
